record.paper_title: On two long standing open problems on Lp-spaces
record.original_question: Let 1 <= p < infinity with p not equal to 2, and let (Omega, Sigma, mu) be a finite atomless measure space such that the density character dim Lp(mu) is strictly larger than aleph_0 and strictly smaller than aleph_{omega_0}. Does Lp(mu) have an unconditional basis, in the nonseparable sense that every element has a unique at most countable unconditional expansion over the basis family?

evidence.quote: A (not ordered) family (xi)i in I of elements of a (non-separable) Banach space X is called an unconditional basis of X if every x in X admits a unique representation x = sum_i in I ai xi, where the set of all indices i in I with ai 6= 0 is at most countable, and the series converges unconditionally.

Problem 5 (P. Enflo and H.P. Rosenthal, 1973, [13]). Let 1 <= p < infinity, p 6= 2, and let (Omega, Sigma, mu) be a finite atomless measure space with aleph_0 < dim Lp(mu) < aleph_omega0. Is there an unconditional basis of Lp(mu)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a real number $p$ with $1 \le p < \infty$ and $p \neq 2$. Let $(\Omega, \Sigma, \mu)$ be a finite atomless measure space, and consider the Banach space $L^p(\mu)$. Assume that the density character (i.e., the smallest cardinality of a dense subset) of $L^p(\mu)$ satisfies
$$\aleph_0 \;<\; \dim L^p(\mu) \;<\; \aleph_{\omega_0}.$$
A family $(x_i)_{i \in I}$ (not necessarily ordered) of nonzero vectors in a Banach space $X$ is called an unconditional basis of $X$ if every $x \in X$ admits a unique representation
$$x = \sum_{i \in I} a_i\, x_i,$$
where $\{i \in I : a_i \neq 0\}$ is at most countable and the series converges unconditionally.

Question: Does $L^p(\mu)$ admit an unconditional basis in this sense?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem, posed by Enflo and Rosenthal in 1973, asks about the existence of an unconditional basis in nonseparable $L^p(\mu)$ for density characters strictly between $\aleph_0$ and $\aleph_{\omega_0}$. Enflo–Rosenthal showed that $L^p(\mu)$ fails to have an unconditional basis when the density character is at least $\aleph_{\omega_0}$, but the intermediate cardinal range remains unresolved in the literature; it is listed as a long-standing open problem.

status_evidence.title: Some results concerning Lp(μ)-spaces - Enflo, Rosenthal
status_evidence.snippet: Lp(μ) does not have an unconditional basis if the cardinality of Lp(μ) is sufficiently large and μ is a finite measure.
status_evidence.claim: Enflo–Rosenthal established nonexistence of unconditional bases for sufficiently large density character, leaving intermediate cardinals open.

status_evidence.claim: The problem is identified as a long-standing open problem.
